title: Blender local submesh restore and transfer
summary: Restore or transfer a verified local Blender submesh from an accepted backup or topology-compatible source without rolling back unrelated current work. Use connected-component/subgraph identity, topology correspondence, exact Basis/Shape Key copying for rollback, or boundary-anchored local mapping for source-shape transfer, then verify target equality/locality and preserved geometry.

intents: restore one damaged Blender submesh from an accepted backup while preserving all unrelated current edits
transfer a local surface or accessory shape from a topology-compatible source model into the current fitted model
repair straps, rings, shoe patches, clothing patches, or other local geometry with Shape Keys without whole-file rollback
constraints: Use only when the target submesh can be identified and source-to-current topology correspondence can be proven.
Keep the reference/backup read-only; mutate only the active working file.
This skill is not a remeshing or arbitrary retopology procedure; if topology differs without a proven mapping, stop before coordinate transfer.

procedure.instruction: Preserve or select an accepted checkpoint/reference and define the exact local target to restore or transfer. Do not use whole-file rollback when unrelated current edits must survive.

Locate the target using connected components, adjacency, material/weight context, or a traced subgraph. Do not rely on object name, bounding box, nearest point, or a screenshot alone when the target is embedded in a larger mesh.

Verify source↔current correspondence before copying coordinates. Check component vertex count, adjacency/degree structure, and component-local ordering. Global indices may differ after unrelated component deletion; derive an offset or local mapping only when topology proves it.

Choose exact restore when the target should match the accepted backup: copy absolute target coordinates. Choose transfer when the current fit/placement must be preserved but source local shape should return: map the source patch into the current frame using corresponding fixed boundary/anchor vertices.

For local transfer, pin patch boundaries, seams, silhouette anchors, connectors, or neighboring accepted geometry unless explicitly in scope. Apply only the interior/reference-shape change needed to reconstruct the target.

If Shape Keys exist, handle the same target indices in every matching key. For exact restore, copy absolute coordinates for Basis/current mesh and all keys from the reference. For intentional deformation, apply the same vertex delta to each corresponding key. Verify key names/order before mutation.

After mutation, verify the target matches the intended reference or mapped result and that non-target geometry stayed unchanged. For exact restore, require near-zero target coordinate delta to the backup; for preserved areas, compare vertex counts, coordinates, or hashes when practical.

Keep the accepted checkpoint available until the user accepts the new local result. If a later experiment fails, restore only the affected verified submesh rather than reconstructing earlier accepted work from memory.
